title: $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-coefficient smooth base change
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. In the Cartesian square [sbc-def-base-change-square]
$$\begin{array}{ccc}Y&\xrightarrow{e}&T\\ h\downarrow&&\downarrow g\\ X&\xrightarrow{f}&S,\end{array}$$
assume $f$ smooth, $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, all four schemes noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ invertible on $S$, as required by the finite-stage coefficient theorem. Use $\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] and the ambient complete coefficient categories of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]. Assume the hypotheses of ambient $E$-coefficient smooth base change [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] hold for every finite-stage representative under consideration and are preserved by passage to a common finite overfield. In particular, $K\in\Dbc(T,\Qlb)$ has a representative $(E,K_E)$ admitting a finite-level etale admissible lattice [sbc-def-admissible-lattices].

The completed direct images and inverse images, evaluated at finite stages and descended by their scalar-extension comparisons, give an exchange isomorphism
$$
 Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},\Qlb}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},\Qlb}K
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},\Qlb}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},\Qlb}K
 \quad\text{in }D_{\mathrm{comp}}(X,\Qlb).
$$
It is represented at stage $E$ by the image of the canonical raw $E$-coefficient exchange under the identity-idempotent inclusion into the ambient Karoubi category, and at every common finite overfield by its coefficient extension. The construction is independent of the common stage (and of the chosen admissible lattice). No constructible landing of the ambient direct images is asserted.

proof.text: Use [lem-sbc-finite-stage-rational-exchange-coherence] for the given square. It gives the actual finite-stage operations, their composite comparisons $b^F,b^G$, and the canonical exchange $\alpha_E$, with normalized unit, tower and exchange equations. Write $F_E=Lf^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}Rg_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}$ and $G_E=Rh_{*,\mathrm{comp},E}Le^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}$; both take values on $X$.

source.place: Qbar_l smooth base change, lines 1439-1455; finite-stage and pair constructions, lines 1191-1359 and 1412-1438

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] to these four operation families and to their exchange. Its composition clause identifies the descended composites with the required two operations. A morphism $[M,u]$ is sent by $F$ to $[M,(b^F_{M/F})^{-1}F_M(u)b^F_{M/E}]$, and similarly by $G$. The exchange component is $[E,\alpha_E(K_E)]$; outer Karoubi extension gives a natural transformation in the ambient category of [def-sbc-ambient-complete-coefficient-categories]. Thus it is the specified canonical exchange.

source.place: Qbar_l smooth base change, lines 1439-1455; finite-stage and pair constructions, lines 1191-1359 and 1412-1438

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], choose $K=(E,K_E)$ and its finite-level etale admissible lattice $(L,\iota)$ from [sbc-def-admissible-lattices]. Here $L_n=L\otimes^L_{\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_T$ has a bounded constructible etale antecedent for every $n\geq0$. The hypotheses give smooth $f$, qcqs $g$, four noetherian schemes, finite-dimensional $X,T$, and invertible $\ell$ on $S$. Hence [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change] gives the raw canonical exchange and a raw inverse $v_E$ at $K_E$, independent of the lattice. The ambient finite-stage category is its Karoubi envelope, not an identified raw category.

source.place: Qbar_l smooth base change, lines 1439-1455; finite-stage and pair constructions, lines 1191-1359 and 1412-1438

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-common-stage-inverse-through-karoubi] to the raw families of step 1 and $v_E$, with both projectors identities. Its inverse formula gives the inverse of the descended component in the ambient outer Karoubi category. Its scalar-conjugation formula identifies every common-overfield representative with that field's canonical exchange; its presentation formula identifies the component for any isomorphic presentation of $K$. The common-stage preservation assumption permits the finite-E theorem at those representatives. Lattice independence follows from [sbc-thm-e-coefficient-smooth-base-change]. These are ambient inverse equations and impose no constructible direct-image landing.
